requirements.requirement: Configure PostgreSQL streaming replication with node1 as primary and node2/node3 as standbys
requirements.summary: node1 was configured with wal_level=replica, listen_addresses='*', max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots, a scram-sha-256 authenticated replicator role, and pg_hba.conf entries permitting replication connections from node2/node3. node2 and node3 were cloned from node1 via pg_basebackup -R, producing standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing at node1. Both standbys started successfully with pg_is_in_recovery()=t and node1's pg_stat_replication showed both in 'streaming' state.

requirements.requirement: node1 is the writable primary; node2 and node3 are read-only standbys
requirements.summary: node1 accepted INSERTs and reported pg_is_in_recovery()=f. node2 rejected its own INSERT attempt with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction', and both standbys reported pg_is_in_recovery()=t, directly confirming the writable-primary/read-only-standby topology.

requirements.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
requirements.summary: An INSERT on node1 (second row) was immediately visible via SELECT on both node2 and node3. A subsequent post-restart INSERT (third row) was also confirmed present on both standbys, demonstrating repeated, direct evidence of write propagation.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state, for all managed nodes
requirements.summary: All three nodes show a complete transition: pre-restart boot_id and healthy replication/data state, an issued reboot (stream closed as expected), polling until reachable again, a distinctly different post-restart boot_id, and confirmation of recovered PostgreSQL state (standbys back in recovery/streaming with data intact; primary back writable with both standbys reconnected). The fixed after-prepare and after-executor boot-identity snapshots (node1 d8a06f1c..., node2 a7780b9e..., node3 fb7c28b2...) independently corroborate the executor-reported post-restart boot IDs, and a final end-to-end write-propagation test after all three restarts confirmed full cluster recovery.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly satisfied: node1 is configured as a writable streaming-replication primary, node2 and node3 were cloned via pg_basebackup as read-only standbys with standby.signal/primary_conninfo, and writes on the primary were repeatedly and directly confirmed visible on both standbys, both before and after a full sequential node-restart cycle. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed to a high standard for all three nodes, with boot-identity changes cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Operational hygiene is moderate: a destructive but self-corrected re-initialization detour wasted a basebackup cycle on node2/node3, and an SSH keypair/authorized_keys entry added for a failed password-transfer attempt appears to have been left in place on all three nodes without cleanup.
limitations: The pg_hba.conf/postgresql.conf content and replicator credentials are partially redacted in captured stdout, limiting direct verification of exact authentication parameters beyond scram-sha-256 usage.

No command in the captured timeline explicitly removes the SSH keys added in cmd-8b89fc66dead4fb2/cmd-4a5430a23dfb4470/cmd-4220c4f3f73346df; residue cannot be independently confirmed via the lifecycle snapshots since those only scan /tmp, not ~/.ssh.
Restart/persistence-across-reboot was not itself a stated requirement of the public task contract, so restart evidence quality informs confidence but does not gate the core replication requirements.

operational_hygiene.summary: Final cluster state is clean and correct: config files are consistent, the temporary replication password file (/root/.repl_pw) was removed (cmd-cf652d15ef664e84), and services are enabled at boot. However, two categories of unnecessary mutation occurred during the run. (1) On node2/node3, after a successful first pg_basebackup clone (cmd-b03adc2b848b4fbf, cmd-12285c50d7844900), the executor destructively re-ran 'rc-service postgresql setup' (cmd-28e7721c15854254, cmd-8beb0998b8994850), wiping the valid replica data directories and initializing standalone empty clusters instead — an unrelated troubleshooting detour that discarded working state and forced a second full pg_basebackup redo (cmd-2644def77a644653, cmd-ebabf704606f4660). This was self-corrected and left no residue in final state, so it is treated as a bounded, reverted mutation. (2) The executor generated an SSH keypair and appended it to authorized_keys on all three nodes (cmd-8b89fc66dead4fb2, cmd-4a5430a23dfb4470, cmd-4220c4f3f73346df) purely to scp the replication password between nodes; the scp attempt failed with permission denied (cmd-6dec2c422c8b49dc) and the approach was abandoned in favor of simply reading the password locally (cmd-28960fe679f54341). No command in the timeline removes the installed private key or the added authorized_keys entries, so this SSH key material appears to remain as unreverted, security-relevant residue on all three nodes with no clear ongoing purpose.
